_comment: No explicit builder: Railway's current default is Railpack, and pinning the older NIXPACKS
here is what made the first deploy fail before it produced a single build log line.
--include=dev is required, not optional. Railway sets NODE_ENV=production, which makes npm
skip devDependencies — and typescript lives there, so the compile step below would have
Plain node against compiled JS, NOT `tsx worker/index.ts`. tsx is a devDependency, and
Railway prunes devDependencies for the runtime image — so a tsx start command works locally
and then dies with 'tsx: not found' in production. Compiling at build time keeps TypeScript
out of the runtime path entirely.
